items.q: Match the drug categories affecting thyroid function tests — 1) Deiodinase inhibitors 2) Enzyme inducers (↑ hormone metabolism) … A) Steroids, Propranolol, Iodine, Amiodarone, Propylthiouracil B) Phenytoin, Carbamazepine, Rifampicin, Sertraline, Ritonavir
items.exp: Deiodinase inhibitors listed are steroids, propranolol, iodine, amiodarone, PTU; enzyme inducers increasing metabolism are phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, sertraline, ritonavir. (Book p904)

items.q: Which of the following drugs is NOT listed on page 904 as a deiodinase inhibitor?
items.exp: Rifampicin is an enzyme inducer that increases hormone metabolism; steroids, propranolol, iodine, amiodarone, and PTU are deiodinase inhibitors. (Book p904)

items.q: Match the drug to its specific effect on thyroid hormone economy — 1) Lithium 2) Al(OH)3, Cholestyramine, Calcium carbonate, Ferrous sulfate … A) Directly causes hypothyroidism B) Decreases thyroid hormone absorption
items.exp: Lithium causes hypothyroidism, while aluminum hydroxide, cholestyramine, calcium carbonate, and ferrous sulfate decrease thyroid hormone absorption. (Book p904)

items.q: What is the normal reference range for TSH tested by 4th-generation CLIA as specified on page 904?
items.exp: Page 904 states: 'TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) : 0.5 - 5 mIU/L (by CLIA 4th generation)'. (Book p904)

items.q: Regarding thyroid testing rules on page 904: I Clinicians should always look for all three: fT3, fT4, and TSH. II Thyroid function tests should not be checked in critically ill patients.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Under TESTS: 'Always look for all of: fT3, fT4, TSH' and 'Do not check in critically ill patients'. (Book p904)

items.q: A patient's laboratory report reveals: TSH elevated (↑), while total T4, free T4, total T3, and free T3 are all normal (N). What is the condition?
items.exp: TSH ↑ with normal T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 represents Subclinical 1° hypothyroidism. (Book p904)

items.q: In overt primary hypothyroidism (TSH ↑, T4 ↓, FT4 ↓, T3 ↓, FT3 ↓), what is the most common etiology and clinical association noted on page 904?
opts: Autoimmune etiology, associated with Hashimoto's thyroiditis
Dietary iodine deficiency, associated with endemic goiter
Consumptive hemangioma, associated with deiodinase-3 excess
Pituitary mass lesion, associated with Sheehan syndrome
items.exp: For primary hypothyroidism, page 904 notes: 'm/c : Autoimmune' and 'A/w : Hashimoto's thyroiditis'. (Book p904)

items.q: A patient's thyroid panel shows elevation of all parameters: TSH ↑, T4 ↑, FT4 ↑, T3 ↑, and FT3 ↑. Clinically, the patient is euthyroid. What is the diagnosis?
items.exp: When TSH, T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 are all elevated, the condition is RTH if the patient is euthyroid, or TSH-secreting adenoma if toxic features are present. (Book p904)

items.q: When TSH, T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 are all simultaneously elevated, match the clinical presentation to the diagnosis — 1) Euthyroid state 2) Toxic features present … A) RTH (Resistance to Thyroid Hormone) B) TSH secreting adenoma
items.exp: For elevated TSH + elevated T4/FT4/T3/FT3: RTH presents as euthyroid; TSH secreting adenoma presents with toxic features. (Book p904)

items.q: In hypothalamo-pituitary (secondary) hypothyroidism: I TSH is normal or decreased (N/↓). II T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 are all decreased (↓).
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: In hypothalamo-pituitary hypothyroidism, TSH is normal or low (N/↓) while peripheral hormones T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 are all low (↓). (Book p904)

items.q: A patient has TSH ↓, total T4 normal, free T4 ↑, total T3 normal, and free T3 ↑. Which causes does the page 904 interpretation table list for this pattern?
opts: Overworking gland (Autoimmune Graves) or stored hormone release (Thyroiditis, Hydatidiform mole/pregnancy)
Subclinical hypothyroidism or sick euthyroid syndrome
items.exp: Under thyrotoxicosis (TSH ↓, T4 N, FT4 ↑, T3 N, FT3 ↑), causes include overworking gland (Autoimmune Graves) and stored hormone release (Thyroiditis, Hydatidiform mole/pregnancy). (Book p904)

items.q: Serum thyroglobulin is elevated in all forms of thyrotoxicosis EXCEPT ___, where exogenous hormone suppresses endogenous thyroglobulin release.
items.exp: Serum thyroglobulin is increased in all thyrotoxicosis except thyrotoxicosis factitia (hormone supplementation). (Book p904)
